newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade active at $64 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade active at $64 -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle early Wednesday were trading actively at $64.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from last week, feedlot sources said.
About 15,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 10,000 in Kansas at the $64.00 price, sources in those areas said.
Total volume was expected to be much larger by the end of the day, sources said.
Fed cattle prices were pressured by a several-day slide in beef prices, sources and analysts noted. However, the drop sparked fairly brisk beef sales.

Beef prices Tuesday fell $0.42 to $1.52 per cwt on 321 fabricated loads sold, compared with the previous day, USDA said. The price on lighter-weight choice beef fell $4.09 in the past week to $98.52 on Tuesday, down from $102.61 a week earlier, USDA statistics showed.
